title: Designing liquid‐core hydrogel beads from fermented fish sauce: structure–function relationships and sensory perception
content:
Abstract

Background

Colatura di alici is a fish sauce traditionally marketed as liquid condiment. This study investigated direct spherification as a means of producing standardized, portionable beads intended primarily for culinary and food-service applications, including plated garnishes and localized delivery of salty and umami flavor.

Results

A Plackett–Burman design screened five formulation and process variables, identifying sodium alginate concentration and gelling time as the main factors affecting bead sphericity. These factors were subsequently investigated using a central composite design. All formulations produced nearly spherical beads with diameters ranging from 3.73 to 4.96 mm. Increasing alginate concentration from 1.2% to 1.6% (w/v) markedly increased hardness and gumminess and reduced swelling capacity from 66% to 28%. Longer gelling times produced smaller reductions in swelling and modest changes in shape regularity. Multi-response optimization identified conditions of approximately 1.38% alginate and 125 s gelling time, predicting intermediate hardness (~0.88 N), low gumminess, a low sphericity index (~0.10), and moderate swelling (~52%). Quantitative descriptive analysis conducted by nine trained assessors showed a progression from more adhesive and red beads at low alginate concentration to firmer beads with greater saltiness, aroma intensity, and anchovy flavor at high alginate concentration. The optimized formulation showed intermediate sensory intensities.

Conclusion

Direct spherification can convert Colatura di alici into a reproducible and portionable condiment format with tunable textural, swelling, and sensory properties. The resulting beads are principally suited to culinary and food-service applications requiring controlled portioning and distinctive presentation. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.
